viz.readAloudUnavailable: Read aloud is not supported in isiXhosa. Browsers cannot speak isiXhosa, so this would mispronounce the lesson.
viz.indexWholeNumber: The index must be a whole number, like 3 or -1.
viz.walkingForward: We are counting from the left, starting at 0, not 1. That is how Python numbers characters. We have now taken {steps} steps and we are on the character '{char}'.
viz.walkingForwardOne: We are counting from the left, starting at 0, not 1. That is how Python numbers characters. We have taken 1 step and we are on the character '{char}'.
viz.countingBack: We are counting from the right, because a negative position counts backwards. The last character is minus 1. We have now counted to {steps} and we are on the character '{char}'.
viz.landedOn: We stopped at position {index}. The character in that box is '{char}'. That is the answer.
viz.ranOut: Ran out of boxes. {index} is outside the valid range.
viz.whyLanded: Here is why. You asked for text[{requested}]. Every character has two names: {pos} if you count from the start, and {neg} if you count from the end. Both names point at the same character, '{char}'. The string has {length} characters, so counting starts at 0 and the last position from the left is {last}.
viz.indexErrorWhy: This is an IndexError, which means the position is not inside the string. The text "{text}" has {length} characters, so the allowed positions are {min} through {max}. You asked for {index}, which is not in that list. Python cannot give you a character, so it reports this error instead of an answer.
viz.valueErrorWhy: This is a ValueError. The step cannot be 0. A step of 0 would mean never move, so Python would be stuck and the slice would never finish. That is why it reports this error instead of giving you a piece of the string.
viz.whyCollecting: A slice copies a piece of the string. It starts at the start position and takes that character. It stops before the stop position, so the stop character is left out. The step is how many places to jump each time.
viz.whySliceClamped: One position you typed is past the end of the string. Slicing does not crash when that happens. Python quietly moves that position to the edge of the string and copies whatever is left. Indexing would have given an IndexError instead.
viz.twoAddressesBefore: This box has two addresses: index
viz.indexErrorTitle: IndexError: string index out of range
viz.sliceWholeNumbers: Start, stop and step must be whole numbers (or left blank for the default).
viz.collecting: Copying the character at position {index}, which is '{char}'. We jump by {step} each time.
viz.collected: Finished. We copied {count} characters, from positions {indices}, in that order. The result is those characters joined together.
viz.collectedOne: Finished. We copied 1 character, from position {indices}. That single character is the whole result.
viz.collectedNone: Finished. We copied no characters, so the result is an empty string.
viz.sliceEmpty: An empty result is not an error. A slice is allowed to copy nothing. Indexing would crash if the position was missing, but slicing does not.
viz.sliceNegativeStep: We walked from right to left because the step is negative. That reverses the string. When start and stop are left blank, Python starts at the last character and stops just before the first one.
viz.sliceDefault: The start position is included in the copy. The stop position is not. The step is how far to jump between each character we take.
viz.valueErrorTitle: ValueError: slice step cannot be zero
viz.sliceIdleBefore: Leave boxes blank to use Python's defaults. Try step
viz.indexIdleAfter: or something out of range to see what happens.

visualiser.title: String Visualiser
visualiser.subtitle: Understand how Python strings work, including loops, conditions, and methods.
visualiser.descForLoop: This is turn {n} of {total} in the for loop. A for loop looks at one character at a time, from left to right. Right now the variable c is the character "{ch}", which sits at position {i}. That is happening because the loop walks the string in order and copies each character into c.
visualiser.descWhileTrue: Checking the while condition {cond}. The counter i is {i}, so the condition is true and the loop body runs. We are looking at the character "{ch}" at position {i}. The body keeps running for as long as this check stays true.
visualiser.descWhileFalse: Checking the while condition {cond} again. The counter i is now {i}, so the condition is false. When a while condition is false, Python stops looping. That is why the loop ends here, and there is no next character.
visualiser.whileConditionUnrecognised: This is an error, not a finished loop. The visualiser only understands conditions like i less than 5. It does not understand "{cond}", so it cannot tell whether the loop should run. That is the error: the condition is not in a form this tool can check. Try i < 5.
visualiser.descIfTrue: Checking if {expr}. The answer is true for this string, so Python runs the code under the if. That is why the if body runs. A condition is true when the test matches this string.
visualiser.descIfFalse: Checking if {expr}. The answer is false for this string, so Python skips the code under the if. If there is an else, that is what would run instead. That is why the if body does not run.
visualiser.descIfDone: The if body has already run, because the condition was true. Nothing more is checked on this step.
visualiser.descElseDone: The else branch would run here, because the condition was false. The if body was skipped.
visualiser.narrationIndexError: Position {index} is not inside this string, so Python reports an IndexError.
visualiser.whyIndexPositive: That is the answer because Python counts from the left, starting at 0, not 1. Position 0 is the first character, position 1 is the second, and so on. So position {index} is the character "{char}".
visualiser.whyIndexNegative: That is the answer because a negative position counts from the right. Minus 1 is the last character, minus 2 is the one before that. So {index} is the same box as position {resolved} from the left, which holds the character "{char}".
visualiser.narrationSlice: The slice {slice} copies this piece of the string: "{output}".
visualiser.whySlice: That is the answer because a slice starts at position {start} and includes that character. It stops before position {stop}, so that character is left out. It jumps by {step} each time, and the copied characters are joined in that order.
visualiser.whySliceNegative: That is the answer because a negative step walks from right to left, which reverses the order. It starts at position {start} and includes that character, stops before position {stop}, and jumps by {step} each time.
visualiser.whySliceEmpty: The result is empty because the start never moves towards the stop with this step, so nothing gets copied. An empty slice is not an error. Slicing is allowed to copy nothing. Indexing would crash if the position was missing.
visualiser.whySliceClamped: A position you typed was past the end of the string. Slicing does not crash. Python moves that position to the edge of the string and copies what is left. Indexing would have given an IndexError instead.
visualiser.whyUpper: That is the answer because upper turns every letter into a capital letter. Spaces, digits and punctuation stay as they are. The original string is not changed. Python gives you a new string.
visualiser.whyLower: That is the answer because lower turns every letter into a small letter. Spaces, digits and punctuation stay as they are. The original string is not changed. Python gives you a new string.
visualiser.whyReverse: That is the answer because reverse reads the string from the last character back to the first. That is the same idea as a slice with a step of minus 1.
visualiser.whyStrip: That is the answer because strip removes spaces only from the beginning and the end. Spaces in the middle of the string stay. The original string is not changed.
visualiser.whyTitle: That is the answer because title makes the first letter of each word a capital, and the rest of each word small.
visualiser.whyLen: That is the answer because len counts how many characters are in the string, including spaces. That count is not the same as the last position. The last position is one less than the length, because counting starts at 0.
visualiser.indexNotANumber: This is an error. "{index}" is not a whole number. A position in a string has to be a whole number such as 0 or minus 1. Python cannot look up a character from this, so there is no answer.
visualiser.indexOutOfRange: This is an IndexError: the position is outside the string. The string has {length} characters, so the allowed positions are {min} through {max}. You asked for {index}, which is not in that list. Python cannot return a character, so it reports this error instead of an answer.
visualiser.sliceZeroStep: This is a ValueError: the slice step cannot be 0. A step of 0 would mean never move, so the slice could never finish. That is why Python reports this error instead of giving you a piece of the string.
visualiser.sliceInvalid: This is an error. "{slice}" is not a valid slice. Each of start, stop and step must be a whole number, or left blank for the default. Because this is not in that form, Python cannot build the slice, so there is no result.
visualiser.methodUnsupported: This is an error. '{method}' is not one of the methods this visualiser can show, so nothing was computed. Try upper, lower, strip, title, reverse, or len.
visualiser.couldNotEvaluateDetail: This is an error, not a false answer. Python did not even get as far as true or false. The visualiser could not work out "{expr}". Check for a typing mistake, or an operator this tool does not support. Because the condition could not be checked, the if statement cannot choose a branch.
visualiser.hintWhileLoop: e.g. i < 5  (i starts at 0, increments by 1)
